title: Reformulation Invariance and the Axiomatic Foundations of Inference
summary: Maximum entropy, Bayesian updating, and exponential-family estimation are all instances of a common inference principle: selecting the measure or distribution that minimizes a divergence subject to the available constraints. Which divergence to use is usually decided by analytic convenience, by empirical performance, or by a set of axioms chosen to single it out, leaving open a basic question: why one divergence and not another? We answer it from a single requirement: an inference method should return the same answer whenever the same problem is presented in an equivalent form, for instance,…
